subject.title: Bug:  ignores  config and returns success on media failure

question: Should Feishu local-media allowlist violations use a shared fs/media-root policy and surface as hard failure or explicit partial success, or should OpenClaw add a Feishu-specific `mediaLocalRoots` config surface?
rationale: Both paths change host-file access and user-visible send semantics; current code supports internal roots plumbing but not the reported config surface, and fallback success is currently covered by tests.

options.title: Shared policy plus explicit failure status
options.body: Use the shared fs/media-root policy as the permission source and update Feishu to report allowlist upload failures as hard failure or explicit partial success.

options.title: Feishu-specific config surface
options.body: Add and document `channels.feishu.mediaLocalRoots` with security-reviewed schema, tests, and migration expectations.

options.title: Keep fallback and document staging
options.body: Treat fallback link delivery as expected behavior and document managed staging directories instead of adding a new root config.

recommendation.title: Shared policy plus explicit failure status
recommendation.body: Use the shared fs/media-root policy as the permission source and update Feishu to report allowlist upload failures as hard failure or explicit partial success.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice sits at the shared outbound media access and security-policy boundary where his recent history is strongest.
